name: Synesius Scholasticus
bio: Synesius Scholasticus was a lawyer and epigrammatist of the sixth century AD. A statue of him in Berytus is the subject of an epigram by Joannes Barbocallus in the Planudean Appendix.
This archive carries the 1 epigram ascribed to the poet in the fifth volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Loeb, 1918): Book XVI: 267.

poems.title: Book XVI, 267: On a Picture of Hippocrates
poems.author: Synesius Scholasticus
poems.text: A. From whence was he who placed thee here? B. A Byzantine. A. And his name? B. Eusebius. A. And who art thou? B. Hippocrates of Cos. A. And why did he paint thee? B. In return for his discourses the city gave him the privilege of making my picture. A. And why did he not paint his own portrait? B. Because, by honouring me instead of himself, he gains greater glory.
